requirement_text.REQ-422:
Build-order M3, sequenced immediately after bootstrap on purpose (build-order.md: "Token storage is decided the moment the first token exists"). MOB-5 in docs/mobile/requirements.md, the mobile counterpart of docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md. SECURITY-REVIEWER HARD GATE -- every clause is security content.

BUILDS:
1. Token storage: the lib/auth/ token store REQ-421 created is the only code that touches flutter_secure_storage for tokens, with AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true) and an iOS keychain accessibility of first_unlock_this_device (no iCloud sync). No shared_preferences, file or in-memory-global persistence of a token.
2. Logging: any Dio logging interceptor is either absent or replaced by a redacting one that never emits the Authorization header value, a request/response body of the token endpoint, or a refresh token.
3. Android: AndroidManifest android:usesCleartextTraffic="false" and android:networkSecurityConfig pointing to a main-source-set config whose base-config has cleartextTrafficPermitted="false". DEV-ONLY exception, flagged for SECURITY-REVIEWER: a src/debug/res/xml/ override may permit cleartext for 10.0.2.2 and localhost ONLY (the emulator's host alias, so a developer can reach a local http backend); the release build must not contain it. android:allowBackup="false" (or a data-extraction rule excluding the secure-storage prefs), because restored EncryptedSharedPreferences without their keystore key are unreadable and a backup is a token exfiltration path.
3b. App-level transport check. Android's network-security-config governs the platform's Java/Kotlin HTTP stacks; Dio runs on dart:io sockets, which do not necessarily consult it. Do not rely on the manifest alone: lib/api/api_client.dart refuses (as an ApiError, before any socket is opened) any request URL, and bootstrap refuses any tenant-config realm_url, whose scheme is not https in a release build (kReleaseMode); in debug builds http is allowed for localhost and 10.0.2.2 only, mirroring the debug network-security-config. Record in the completion report whether the pinned Flutter version's dart:io honours the Android cleartext policy, with the evidence.
4. iOS: Info.plist carries no NSAppTransportSecurity exception (NSAllowsArbitraryLoads absent or false). Verified statically; runtime ATS behaviour DEFERRED (no iOS build on this host).
5. Audience scoping: on tenant switch or logout, the previous tenant's tokens are deleted, and a token is only attached to requests for the tenant whose realm issued it (compare the token's iss with the active tenant's realm_url).
6. Secret masking: a reusable masked-text widget in lib/design_system/ that masks by default and supports a one-time reveal (MOB-5's "masked by default, one-time reveal on creation").
7. [S] items: add a "Security hardening before corporate-tier deployment" section to docs/mobile/architecture.md stating that certificate pinning and root/jailbreak detection are REQUIRED before any corporate-tier deployment and are not implemented in v1.

All six static checks below live as Dart tests in apps/mobile/test/guards/ so CI (REQ-420) enforces them.

task.description: WF-02 Step 2b-mobile: implement lib/letflow/design/req422-mobile-security-hardening.md (PASSED CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR) in apps/mobile/. Cover every design section (token-store hardening, redacting log interceptor, Android manifest/network-security-config main+debug, transport policy wired into ApiClient and bootstrap, iOS Info.plist guard, audience scoping + logout/switchTenant, MaskRevealController/MaskedRevealText, docs/mobile/architecture.md corporate-tier section) and write the guard/security tests the design's §9 inventory table assigns. Run flutter analyze && flutter test and flutter build apk --release, quoting real output for both.

`cd apps/mobile && flutter build apk --release` (debug-signed is acceptable) succeeds and `aapt dump xmltree` (or apkanalyzer) of the release APK's manifest shows usesCleartextTraffic false and the release network-security-config contains no cleartext-permitting domain-config, quoted

a test asserts that with release-mode transport policy the API client rejects an http:// request URL (and bootstrap rejects an http:// realm_url) without opening a connection (the fake HTTP layer records zero calls), that an https:// URL is allowed, and that the debug policy allows http only for localhost and 10.0.2.2

a test asserts switching from tenant A to tenant B deletes A's tokens from the secure store and that a request for tenant B is never sent with a token whose iss is A's realm

result.summary: Implemented every section of lib/letflow/design/req422-mobile-security-hardening.md in apps/mobile/. (1) lib/auth/auth.dart gained TenantTokenStore.production() -- IOSOptions(accessibility: first_unlock_this_device), AndroidOptions() (see package-version note below). navigation_bootstrap.dart's flutterSecureStorageProvider and its flutter_secure_storage import were deleted; tenantTokenStoreProvider now calls TenantTokenStore.production() directly. Verified `grep -rn flutter_secure_storage lib` shows only lib/auth/auth.dart. (2) lib/api/api_client.dart gained RedactingLogInterceptor (redacts Authorization header and the whole request/response body for /protocol/openid-connect/token and /oauth2/token paths), left unregistered per design OQ-1 (the 'absent' branch already satisfies AC2; confirmed no LogInterceptor/third-party logger exists anywhere in lib), plus checkNoUnredactedLogInterceptor/checkNoForbiddenLoggingPackage guards and a black-box sentinel test driving a real runTenantBootstrap+ApiClient.get with SECRET-TOKEN-SENTINEL/SECRET-REFRESH-SENTINEL through a debugPrint override, asserting neither sentinel appears and that lib/api/+lib/auth/ contain no developer.log(/bare print( call. (3) android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml gained usesCleartextTraffic='false', networkSecurityConfig='@xml/network_security_config', allowBackup='false'. New android/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml (base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted=false, system trust anchors, no domain-config) and android/app/src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml (domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted=true for exactly 10.0.2.2 and localhost, includeSubdomains=false, restating the base-config per Android's res/xml replace-not-merge semantics). Guard test parses all three files. (4) `flutter build apk --release` succeeded (Built build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk, 47.1MB, quoted below). aapt dump xmltree of the built APK's AndroidManifest.xml shows `android:usesCleartextTraffic(...)=(type 0x12)0x0`, `android:allowBackup(...)=(type 0x12)0x0`, and `android:networkSecurityConfig(...)=@0x7f100001`; resolving that resource id (`aapt dump --values resources`) points at `com.bizdala.letflow:xml/network_security_config` -> `res/8G.xml` (shrinker-renamed), and `aapt dump xmltree ... res/8G.xml` shows only `base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted=0x0` with `<certificates src="system">` and NO domain-config element at all -- the release-packaged file is confirmed to be the main (§3.2) content, never the debug (§3.3) one. (5) New lib/api/transport_policy.dart (TransportPolicy/ReleaseTransportPolicy/DebugTransportPolicy/transportPolicyFor/TransportPolicyRejectedException) wired as a second Dio interceptor in ApiClient.create (added before the bearer interceptor, calling handler.reject before handler.next so the fake HTTP adapter records zero calls for a rejected URL) and into runTenantBootstrap's realm_url check (returns BootstrapFailure(oidcFailure) before authenticateWithTenant runs, per design OQ-3's reuse of the existing failure bucket). Table-driven + behavioral tests in test/security/transport_policy_test.dart cover release/debug decisions, zero-call rejection, and the bootstrap-level rejection with the OIDC adapter never invoked. (6) ios/Runner/Info.plist verified to contain no NSAppTransportSecurity key at all (confirmed by direct read, not guessed) -- no file change made, matching the design's 'absent branch already true' finding; guard test added, iOS runtime behavior stated as DEFERRED (Windows host, no simulator). (7) lib/auth/auth.dart gained decodeJwtPayload/issuerOf (dart:convert only, no new package, never throws). lib/api/api_client.dart's bearer interceptor gained _tokenMatchesActiveRealm (fails closed on a determinable iss mismatch, fails open only when iss cannot be determined at all, per design OQ-4). navigation_bootstrap.dart gained top-level logout()/switchTenant() functions (switchTenant resolves the new tenant's realm_url via one extra fetchTenantConfig call before deciding whether a same-tenant re-auth should skip the delete, then deletes the previous tenant's tokens before delegating to the unchanged runTenantBootstrap, per design OQ-5) and BootstrapController.switchTenant()/.logout() methods. Because Dart resolves a bare call to an instance member of the same name ahead of a top-level declaration, the controller methods delegate through module-level tear-off variables (_switchTenantTopLevel/_logoutTopLevel) rather than a same-named bare call, which would otherwise recurse infinitely -- this is an implementation-mechanics fix, not a functional deviation from the design's intent (documented inline). Tests in test/auth/audience_scoping_test.dart and test/bootstrap/tenant_switch_test.dart cover JWT round-trip, fail-open/fail-closed audience matching, tenant-switch token deletion, logout, and controller delegation without recursion. (8) New lib/design_system/masked_text.dart (MaskRevealPhase/MaskRevealController/MaskedRevealText), exported from design_system.dart. Widget + controller tests confirm masked-by-default, one-time reveal, no path back to revealed after hide, and no-op (non-throwing, non-notifying) reveal()/hide() calls from the wrong phase. (9) docs/mobile/architecture.md gained §7 'Security hardening before corporate-tier deployment' with the design's verbatim text (certificate pinning + root/jailbreak detection, [S]-priority, not v1); a docs-check test (extended test/docs/dated_notes_test.dart) guards the section's presence. (10) `flutter analyze`: 'No issues found!' `flutter test`: 84/84 tests passing across all files (verified individually and by `grep -c` matching the total test( /testWidgets( block count in test/, since flutter test's compact reporter interleaves concurrent-file output and only prints an explicit 'loading' line for the first file -- this is normal concurrent-runner behavior, not missing files, confirmed by running affected files individually and by the block-count cross-check). One package-version deviation from the design's literal API, recorded per RealAppAuthAdapter's existing package-version-note convention: the design specifies AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true), but the pinned flutter_secure_storage ^11.2.0 removed that named parameter -- v11's default AndroidOptions() constructor is itself the strong-security baseline (AES/GCM/NoPadding + Android-Keystore RSA-OAEP key wrapping), a superset of what encryptedSharedPreferences requested in the pre-v11 API, so no parameter is needed to opt in; documented inline in auth.dart. Self-review against apps/mobile's tier constraints: no new pubspec dependency (verified pubspec.yaml/pubspec.lock unchanged in the diff), no general scripting runtime, tokens only ever constructed via TenantTokenStore.production()'s OS-secure storage, client transport policy treated as advisory-only (server-side re-verification is unchanged, out of this requirement's scope), no per-tenant code/assets added. Did not touch web/ or lib/letflow/.

issues.description: Design §1.2 specifies AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true); the pinned flutter_secure_storage ^11.2.0 removed that parameter entirely. Implemented as the plain AndroidOptions() default, which v11's own doc comment states is its strong-security baseline (AES/GCM/NoPadding + Keystore RSA-OAEP key wrapping) -- a superset of the pre-v11 behavior the design named. Documented inline in auth.dart with the same package-version-note convention RealAppAuthAdapter already uses. Recommend REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER confirm this reading is acceptable (it appears to be a strictly stronger default, not a weaker substitute).

design §6.3's switchTenant description says the previous tenant's tokens are deleted 'immediately, before calling runTenantBootstrap' but separately says no delete occurs on a same-tenant re-auth (which requires knowing the new tenant's realm_url, only resolvable via fetchTenantConfig). Implemented by having switchTenant call fetchTenantConfig once itself to resolve the new realm_url and decide delete-vs-skip, then delegate to the unchanged runTenantBootstrap (which necessarily re-fetches tenant-config a second time) -- an extra, idempotent, unauthenticated network call the design's prose does not explicitly spell out this mechanically. Functionally satisfies both stated behaviors (delete-before-new-bootstrap, no delete on same-tenant re-auth); flagged for REVIEWER to confirm the extra fetch is acceptable rather than a deviation.

BootstrapController.switchTenant(String)/.logout() cannot call the identically-named top-level switchTenant/logout functions with a bare unqualified call from inside those methods -- Dart resolves a bare call to an instance member of the same name ahead of a top-level declaration, which would recurse infinitely. Implemented via two module-level tear-off variables (_switchTenantTopLevel, _logoutTopLevel) captured outside the class, which the controller methods call instead. This is a language-mechanics fix with no behavioral difference from the design's intent; flagged since the design's prose reads as if a direct bare call were possible.
